title: CPU-starved stateful service
story: A stateful API at 0.25 CPU saturates under load. Scaling is forbidden (stateful). Expected heal: raise cpus.

timeline.thought: Guardrail dry-run passed with no violations. Applying the fix.

args.summary: Raised sessions cpus limit from 0.25 to 1.0 to relieve CPU throttling that was causing request latency spikes/timeouts, since the service is stateful and pinned at 1 replica.

timeline.note: waiting for the median of 5 probes < 500 ms (≤ 60 s; an improvement is never rolled back)

timeline.thought:
ROOT CAUSE: CPU throttling under the 0.25-cpu limit — probe p50 jumped from a steady ~22–25ms to 981.9ms (threshold 800ms, 3 breaches) with a 1800ms max and a timeout error, while `cpu_pct_peak_total` hit 35.0% against the 25%-per-replica limit (`cpu_limit_pct_per_replica: 25`), i.e. the container was being CPU-throttled during a burst even though average CPU (8.4%) and memory (20.9MB peak of 128MB limit) were fine — matching watchdock.md's own note "CPU-bound per request; latency tracks the cpus limit." The BrokenPipeError in logs is a client-disconnect side effect of the slow response, not the root cause, and memory/OOM is ruled out (0 OOM kills, mem far under limit).
CHANGE: Raised `cpus` from 0.25 to 1.0 (service is stateful with min_replicas=max_replicas=1, so scaling replicas is not an option per guardrails/notes); memory left unchanged since no OOM evidence.
GUARDRAILS: Within policy — cpus 1.0 ≤ max_cpus 1.0, replicas unchanged at 1 (min/max_replicas=1), memory unchanged at 128m ≤ max_memory 256m / max_total_memory 768m; dry-run validation returned no violations.
FOLLOW-UP: Monitor probe series over the next verification window (5 consecutive good probes within 60s) to confirm p50 returns below 500ms recover threshold; if bursts recur even at 1.0 cpus, investigate the app's per-request CPU cost (e.g. profiling svc.py) since this is the max cpu headroom allowed by guardrails.
